extracted.intended_audience: aspiring fiction writers, MFA students, and practicing novelists/short-story writers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing, revising, and finishing literary fiction (novels and short stories), covering beginnings, daily practice, story shaping, character, style, and revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beginnings
rubrics_metrics.description: How to start; what to capture in early drafts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on getting a workable opening into the draft: capture the initial situation, the inciting tension, memorable detail, and what you discover while writing. Avoid over-polishing openings in a way that blocks discovery. Treat beginnings as exploratory material to be shaped later.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Writing Life
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain discipline: write regularly, keep notebooks, and cultivate reading routines. Notebook discipline and daily practice feed material and craft; read widely and deeply, especially masters of your form, to absorb technique and standards. Anti-patterns: sporadic writing, neglecting notebooks, and not reading enough models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shaping the Story
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the story's spine (central dramatic question) and shape plot as the structure that delivers the story. Use structural choices to clarify stakes and momentum. Avoid imposing plot that contradicts what the story discovers; instead let story discovery inform structural decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making Characters Live
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create characters with rich inner lives and believable exterior behavior: clear desires, obstacles, contradictions, and interiority that extend beyond mere plot function. Show how internal conflicts interact with external situations. Anti-patterns: flat characters who exist only to move plot forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventing Your Style
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop an authentic voice through sentence-level choices (rhythm, diction, cadence) rather than forcing an affected style. Experiment, but allow style to emerge from attention to phrasing and tonal consistency. Examples: pay attention to how master writers handle sentence rhythm; avoid mimicry that reads as imposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Story of the Self
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing from personal material, manage distance and perspective: decide how much self to reveal and transform life into narrative. Balance authenticity with craft, shaping personal events into story while maintaining necessary dramatic distance. Anti-patterns: unprocessed autobiographical dumping or failure to fictionalize detail for dramatic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working and Reworking
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat revision as the core of craft: cut, reorder, and reshape until the story achieves tightness and resonance. Multiple passes are expected; be willing to excise beloved material that doesn't serve the story. Scoring guidance: look for revision evidence in tightened scenes, clarified focus, and emergent patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finishing
rubrics_metrics.description: When and how to stop; recognizing completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize an ending that feels arrived at rather than abruptly stopped. Know when the story's questions have been resolved sufficiently and when further tinkering ceases to add value. Anti-patterns: endless tinkering, premature abrupt endings, or endings that feel grafted-on rather than earned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notebook discipline
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep constant notes — images, lines, observations, scene fragments — to supply raw material for fiction. Use notebooks to preserve discoveries that might otherwise be forgotten. Anti-patterns: relying solely on memory or neglecting to record promising details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fast first drafts
rubrics_metrics.description: Get the bones down; revise later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write early drafts quickly to allow discovery and to prevent premature polishing from blocking new directions. Prioritize momentum and raw structure over line-level perfection in initial passes. Anti-patterns: obsessively revising opening pages, stalling progress through early editing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot serves story, not vice versa
rubrics_metrics.description: Story is what you discover; plot is the structure that delivers it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let the emergent story inform plotting decisions. Use plot to clarify and deliver the discoveries of character and theme rather than forcing events to meet a predetermined plot outline. Anti-patterns: plotting as constraint that overrides character truth or thematic honesty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read widely and deeply
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study exemplary writing to learn possibilities of form, voice, and technique. Emulate to learn, then transform those lessons into your own practice. Reading should be active: analyze sentence rhythms, scene construction, and how authors solve similar problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust the process of revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Early drafts are exploration; final form emerges through cutting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have confidence that rigorous revision will reveal the work's best shape. Be willing to remove material, reorder scenes, and refine language through repeated editing. Evidence of good revision includes increased clarity, tension, and resonant detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style emerges, doesn't get imposed
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow authentic voice to arise rather than force stylistic tricks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop style organically through consistent sentence-level choices and tonal unity. Avoid contrived devices or artificial diction meant to impress; instead cultivate habits that produce an honest, coherent voice. Scoring note: forced or inconsistent style is a negative signal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story has a discoverable spine
rubrics_metrics.description: A central throughline or dramatic question that can be identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the work has a recognizable spine — a problem or question that drives narrative choices and gives scenes purpose. Evaluate whether each scene relates to that spine and whether the spine is clarified by revision. Anti-patterns: diffuse narratives without a guiding dramatic question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characters have inner lives that exceed plot function
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters possess interiority, contradictions, and desires beyond moving the plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create depth by giving characters histories, private thoughts, and motivations that sometimes resist plot demands. This produces believable, three-dimensional figures whose actions feel lived-in. Anti-patterns: schematic characters who exist only to trigger external events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision visible in tightness and resonance
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective revision shows in compressed, resonant prose and structural economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge revision by how scenes feel leaner, images more resonant, and narrative focus clearer. Look for removed redundancies and sharpened causal links. Anti-patterns: drafts that retain exploratory bloat or repetitive passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ending feels arrived at, not stopped
rubrics_metrics.description: Endings should feel earned and inevitable given the story's spine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An effective ending resolves or reframes the dramatic question and stems naturally from character choices and narrative momentum. Avoid tacked-on conclusions, unresolved abruptness, or endings that rely on deus ex machina.
